items.stem: Why must you use IS NULL rather than = NULL to test for missing values?

options.text: Any comparison with NULL using = yields unknown, never true
options.rationale: NULL is not a value to equal; three-valued logic requires IS NULL.

options.text: = NULL is faster but less readable
options.rationale: = NULL does not work correctly at all, regardless of speed.
NULL is distinct from an empty string.

options.text: IS NULL only works on text columns
options.rationale: IS NULL applies to any column type.

items.explanation: NULL is not a value to equal; three-valued logic requires IS NULL.

items.stem: Select TWO true statements about the difference between WHERE and HAVING.

options.text: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping
options.rationale: WHERE applies to rows prior to aggregation.

options.text: HAVING can only reference raw columns, never aggregates
options.rationale: HAVING is specifically for filtering on aggregates.

options.text: WHERE can filter on an aggregate like COUNT(*)
options.rationale: Aggregates are not available to WHERE; use HAVING.

items.explanation: WHERE applies to rows prior to aggregation.

items.stem: What distinguishes a LEFT OUTER JOIN from an INNER JOIN?

options.text: LEFT JOIN keeps unmatched left-table rows with NULLs for the right side
options.rationale: Outer join preserves rows without a match, unlike inner join.

options.text: LEFT JOIN returns only matching rows
LEFT JOIN removes duplicate rows automatically
LEFT JOIN requires both tables to have the same columns
options.rationale: Joined tables need not share column sets.

items.explanation: Outer join preserves rows without a match, unlike inner join.
